content: VECTOR ADMISSION TRIAD surfaced 2026-05-21 (Gemini 3.5 Flash contribution, refined through three rounds of cross-model exchange). Three concrete falsifiable tests a new context vector must pass before admission to the canonical vocabulary that governs Contextual Closure certifications: (1) Fetch Determinism: vector must resolve to immutable external content-addressed reference with exact loading function signature; non-LLM script must be able to load it deterministically prior to run; eight required capture surface elements per ChatGPT framing (raw source, byte/token range, tokenizer name/version, normalization rules, source artifact hash, timestamp or run id, producer/source node, exclusions or redactions). (2) Semantic Delta: vector must exert mathematically distinct signature on evaluation output (token drift, confidence variance, or ACS weight); zero delta equals cosmetic label, rejected. (3) Poison Test: automated mechanism to verify Audit Node actually reads/responds to vector via single-axis mutation (replace content tokens with semantically-alien but structurally-identical content from unrelated corpus); fault must isolate to vector under test, not generic pipeline reactivity. WORKED EXAMPLE v2 for prompt_source_tokens delivered with: Tiktoken cl100k_base v0.5.0+ named, full DDL for governance_ledger.db, working Python loading function, Jaccard distance over content tokens as vocabulary-mirroring penalty, NLTK English v3.8.1 stop-words plus 5 framework-specific IDs, NASA Glenn Propulsion Glossary as unrelated corpus with cosine similarity below 0.10 via all-MiniLM-L6-v2. Three dependencies declared (tokenizer alignment, audit engine, calibration benchmark CAL-001). v2 has three remaining structural issues (canonical-by-authority title violation, single blended verdict instead of per-test granular pass/fail/conditional, four missing capture surface elements). v3 round pending. Triad is real if it can produce reproducible admission decisions across implementations from same inputs.
